data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"An append-only event log requires neither safety nor idempotence of individual writers; it requires commutativity of concurrent appends and idempotence of the deduplication layer. Writers can freely produce duplicate entries; the log's ordering and dedup infrastructure absorbs the redundancy. The at-least-once delivery guarantee is satisfied by the delivery mechanism, not by the writer being idempotent.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the problem specifically asks about writer-level properties (as RFC 9110 scopes them), this systemic answer may not directly address the question.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If dedup is not feasible (unbounded producer identities, no global sequencing), the log cannot survive at-least-once delivery and this claim fails.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In distributed log architectures (e.g., Kafka, event-sourcing systems), producers send events and the broker may duplicate them under at-least-once. The log tolerates this by assigning monotonically increasing sequence numbers per producer epoch; consumers or a compaction step dedup. The writer's HTTP-level idempotence is irrelevant; the system invariant is maintained by the log's own sequencing and dedup. Thus the required property is systemic, not per-writer.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
